races.title: State House, District 18
races.note: The top two finishers from the Nov 3, 2026 count. Everyone else in this race is coming.

cands.name: Latisha Grady
cands.bio: Republican candidate for North Carolina House District 18 in 2026. Her campaign site lists an operations career: Ripple Labs operations specialist, multifamily real estate closings, co-founder of a natural hair company. She was secretary of the Jones County Republican Party 2021-2023. She has held no public office.
cands.gaps: We found no record of any public office held, so there are no votes or official actions to report. We could not read the full text of her campaign blog posts (the WECT forum written answers, the school choice post, the birthright citizenship post, and her District 18 plan); only their titles appeared, so we did not use them. We found no stated positions on data centers, development and growth, homestead property taxes, foreign or investor land buying, guns, abortion, or teacher pay. Her general call for lower tax burdens and attracting businesses did not specifically address any of those topics. Her birthplace, upbringing, return to North Carolina in 2016, and work history come only from her own campaign site, and we found no independent confirmation. Ballotpedia lists no endorsements for her, and she did not complete its candidate survey. We found no controversies or foreign ties.

local.label: Roots 100: Her campaign site says she was born and raised on a tobacco farm in Trenton, near New Bern, lived in Atlanta for a number of years, and returned to North Carolina in 2016.

score.why: Raised $0, under $5,000 for this office: too little money to score fairly.

qual.background: Her campaign site says she has over 15 years in operations and process work for real estate, accounting, HR and fintech teams. It lists a Ripple Labs operations specialist role, closing multifamily real estate deals, co-founding a natural hair company, and freelance administrative work. She was county Republican Party secretary 2021-2023. She has held no elected office.
qual.why: She has business and management-type experience, which fits the middle band. She has no legislative service and no law, policy or budget career. All of this comes from her own site and was not independently confirmed.
qual.label: She has business and management-type experience, which fits the middle band. She has no legislative service and no law, policy or budget career. All of this comes from her own site and was not independently confirmed.

back-police-order.evidence: Her campaign site says she supports local police and cooperation with federal partners so dangerous individuals who commit crime are identified and removed.

school-choice-teachers.evidence: Her campaign site says she supports parental choice in education.

prio.label: Matches 2 of 2 priorities; 0 backed by their record, 2 only promised

roots.summary: Her campaign site says she was born and raised on a tobacco farm in Trenton, near New Bern, lived in Atlanta for a number of years, and returned to North Carolina in 2016.

cands.name: Deb Butler
cands.bio: Deb Butler is a Wilmington attorney and Democrat. Gov. Roy Cooper appointed her to the NC House in February 2017 and she has held District 18 (part of New Hanover County) since. She lost a 2012 State Senate race. She describes herself as a long-time small business owner.

endorsements.text: Sierra Club North Carolina and the Center for Freethought Equality are listed by Ballotpedia among her 2026 endorsements and voter guide recommendations.

cands.gaps: We found no stated position or record from her on data centers, homestead property tax elimination, limits on investor or foreign land buying, or growth and development limits. Her campaign site says county property taxes are rising because Raleigh shifts costs to counties, but it gives no tax-cut pledge. We could not find the year she moved to North Carolina or the town where she grew up. The pages we read showed no specific bills she sponsored and no documented controversies or foreign ties. Her statements come from her own campaign site and Ballotpedia surveys, so we have few independent records of what she has done.

local.label: Roots 90: Ballotpedia lists her birthplace as Columbia, SC, and her campaign site says she was raised in North Carolina; she has practiced law in Wilmington and served in the NC House since 2017.

score.why: Raised $0, under $5,000 for this office: too little money to score fairly.

qual.background: Attorney (Wake Forest J.D., 1986) and self-described small business owner. NC House member since 2017. By her own account she became Democratic Whip after the 2018 election. Ran for State Senate in 2012.
qual.why: Nine years of legislative service and a law career fit a job of writing law and the budget. Committee seats were not counted. The whip role is her own account and is held in the minority party.
qual.label: Nine years of legislative service and a law career fit a job of writing law and the budget. Committee seats were not counted. The whip role is her own account and is held in the minority party.

second-amendment.evidence: Her campaign site says she supports renewing the federal assault weapons ban, universal background checks, safe storage and extreme risk protective orders (red-flag laws).

pro-life.evidence: Her campaign site says she supports codifying Roe v. Wade and that women should control their own bodies.

workers-first.evidence: Her campaign site criticizes the Trump administration's use of ICE and Border Patrol for warrantless searches of immigrants, calling it racial profiling that hampers local law enforcement. She calls for comprehensive reform by Congress.

clean-money.evidence: Her campaign site says money in politics is corrupting the process and that she supports fundraising caps and full transparency. It does not pledge to refuse any particular donors.

back-police-order.evidence: Her campaign site says police need additional personnel and training so officers can focus on policing, alongside efforts to reduce racial bias.

prio.label: Matches 2 of 5 priorities; 0 backed by their record, 2 only promised
